name: Kelvin-Helmholtz Billows
desc: Two dyed fluid layers slide past each other and roll their shear interface into the iconic train of breaking cat's-eye billows, curling and advecting forever on the clock as warm cloud over cool sky, teal ocean foam, thermal false-color, indigo ink, or luminous aurora curtains.

billow.doc: shear-instability amplitude — 0 flat sliding layers, 1 deep curled cat's-eye vortices

scale.doc: billow size / wavelength (higher = fewer, bigger rolls)

shear.doc: sliding speed + interface confinement (higher = faster, sharper roll-up)

hue.doc: palette base hue (rotates warm layer, cool auto-complements)

x.doc: horizontal phase bias of the billow train

y.doc: mean height of the shear interface

act.doc: multi-minute program: steady drift / laminar-to-rolled build / turbulent storm

alpha.doc: opacity for VJ compositing (100 = opaque bg)
